summary:
What we built: A 3D Mars exploration game in a single HTML file that runs in any browser. Players guide an astronaut to find five real NASA spacecraft across three levels with a shrinking oxygen timer. Along the way they use a radar, fight alien guards, collect coins and shop for upgrades.

How it solves the challenge: It turns learning into a mission. Each spacecraft unlocks an animated story, followed by a quiz. Wrong answers show the story fact again instead of just failing, and optional voice narration reads everything aloud.

Why it matters: It makes the history of Mars exploration engaging instead of lecture-style. It needs no installation, and it supports visual, audio and hands-on learning styles.
details: Mars Expedition is an interactive, browser-based STEM educational game that combines engaging gameplay with authentic NASA mission history. When players discover a collectible spacecraft, gameplay and oxygen depletion pause to launch a multi-chapter storytelling modal featuring custom 2D animations, authentic NASA archival photos, and built-in Text-to-Speech voice narration. To reinforce learning without frustration, each story is followed by a zero-penalty quiz where wrong answers trigger gentle encouragement and re-display the relevant fact rather than penalizing the player. Discovering spacecraft and acing quizzes reward players with coins, which can be spent in the Space Shop on strategic upgrades like extra oxygen tanks, a directional search radar, a speed-boosting spacesuit, and a heavy laser cannon. Grounded in real missions—including Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner, Viking 1, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—the lightweight app runs smoothly via Three.js, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and dynamic Web Audio API soundscapes. Looking ahead, Mars Expedition aims to expand into a multi-planetary learning platform covering missions like Artemis, Europa Clipper, and Titan, integrating real NASA terrain maps and classroom multiplayer modes to inspire the next generation of space explorers.
